provenance.fixture: dataset_monstree/mini6 (configuration above, enforced by the runner). The candidate global mapper runs with RotationAveragingBackend::CERES via GlobalMapper.ra_backend; the upstream baseline has no rotation-averaging backend CLI knob (RotationEstimatorOptions), so this gate measures the fork CERES production path against the upstream global pipeline, not backend parity.
provenance.rule: Count metrics are discrete, so any difference is algorithmic and the threshold is 0. Each continuous threshold is the log-space midpoint sqrt(lower_input * upper_input), rounded to one significant digit. It is never fitted to the candidate.

lower_input.method: The measured cross-binary divergence of the CERES variant is the effective noise floor of this comparison: two repeated runs were bit-identical (candidate metrics and model identical across runs), so the fork-CERES/upstream delta below is stable and reproducible, not run noise
lower_input.notes: The rotation delta was measured as exactly 0, so the acos resolution near identity (acos(1 - 2^-53) = 8.5e-7 deg) is used as the lower input. CERES and upstream L1 rotation averaging converge to the identical structure (counts, mean track length and rotations are identical); the deltas are final-BA residuals.

smallest_algorithmic_divergence.method: Upper input = smallest real algorithmic perturbation measured on this fixture (incremental pipeline, std::unordered hash containers versus upstream boost::unordered 1.92, i.e. SfM gauge and BA residual-order divergence). A real CERES-path regression is expected at or above this scale

provenance.scope: Same-host gate only. A different CPU, compiler, or BLAS can move the floating-point floor and requires re-measuring both inputs of the rule.
